I always have believed in just standing by your word, don't be a dick (and if you were being a dick apologize). I think it's always important to remember intentions, or what is call "malice aforethough", if the comments made were thought about and meant to cause harm.

I caught myself once talking to a relative who'd asked me for directions to somewhere and I said, "No you don't want to go that way, that's a gay way to take" or something, and I was really embarrassed but he laughed and I laughed because it was obvious I wasn't trying to be a dick.

Offensiveness given is usually pretty obvious, but one cannot control how the human brain of another will interpolate and decode the message through their own personal filter. They have the right to be offended about whatever they like, but without "malice aforethought" you can't hold someone else punitively accountable - you can have a discussion about it, which is a good thing and helps us all to understand - and I've come to realize that nobody wants to punish those who say things innocently. Reason always wins out in the end.
